title: Wayward
synopsis: Your daughter is enrolled at Tall Pines Academy, the troubled-teen 'school' on the edge of a town where every adult smiles the same way. By morning you'll wish you'd never read the brochure.

nodes.text: The 'Welcome to Wayward' sign is hand-painted and the smile of the diner waitress is hand-painted too. Your daughter pretends to sleep in the passenger seat. Tall Pines Academy is two miles uphill. The paths divide here: “Stop at the diner first” leads into The Diner, while “Drive straight to the academy” makes The Gates the next reckoning.

choices.text: Stop at the diner first
choices.consequence: Eavesdrop before you enroll. You commit to stop at the diner first. It carries you into The Diner while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Drive straight to the academy
choices.consequence: Delay is doubt's open door. You commit to drive straight to the academy. It carries you into The Gates while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Three locals stop talking when you walk in. The waitress is friendly in a way that feels rehearsed. A boy in his early twenties keeps glancing at your bumper sticker. “Try to make conversation about the academy” opens the route to The Tour. “Eat quickly and leave” changes the terms and carries you toward The Sheriff.

choices.text: Try to make conversation about the academy
choices.consequence: Information lives in small talk. You try to make conversation about the academy. The way toward The Tour opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Eat quickly and leave
choices.consequence: Some rooms tighten if you stay. You commit to eat quickly and leave. It carries you into The Sheriff while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Wrought iron, freshly painted. A counselor named Evelyn meets you with a clipboard and a hug she has practiced. Your daughter's hand is suddenly very cold in yours. The paths divide here: “Sign the intake forms quickly” leads into The Tour, while “Ask to see the dorm first” makes The Sheriff the next reckoning.

choices.text: Sign the intake forms quickly
choices.consequence: You came here to do this. You choose to sign the intake forms quickly. By The Tour, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Ask to see the dorm first
choices.consequence: Trust earned beats trust assumed. You choose to ask to see the dorm first. By The Sheriff, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The grounds are beautiful in a sterilized way — every flower planted, every kid smiling the moment a counselor passes. A girl walks the path with her eyes carefully forward, like she is being graded on it.

choices.text: Stop and speak to one of the students
choices.consequence: A real face will tell you more than the tour. You commit to stop and speak to one of the students. It carries you into The Girl in the Garden while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Stay on the script of the tour
choices.consequence: Don't tip your suspicion yet. You commit to stay on the script of the tour. It carries you into Lights Out Tour while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The sheriff happens to be at the gate, friendly, broad. He compliments your car. He mentions that 'parents who second-guess' tend to make things harder for their kids. The paths divide here: “Smile and play along for now” leads into The Girl in the Garden, while “Ask him bluntly what he meant” makes Lights Out Tour the next reckoning.

choices.text: Smile and play along for now
choices.consequence: Don't show your hand to the law. You smile and play along for now. The way toward The Girl in the Garden opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Ask him bluntly what he meant
choices.consequence: Some bluffs collapse if you call them. You ask him bluntly what he meant. The way toward Lights Out Tour opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Choose “Take her warning seriously” and The Missing Kid comes into view; choose “Wonder if she's manipulating you” and the road bends toward Your Daughter Whispers. In The Girl in the Garden, even a sensible delay gives the threat another way in.

choices.text: Take her warning seriously
choices.consequence: Truth from a child here is gold. You commit to take her warning seriously. It carries you into The Missing Kid while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Wonder if she's manipulating you
choices.consequence: Suspicion can also be useful here. You choose to wonder if she's manipulating you. By Your Daughter Whispers, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Evelyn explains the nightly schedule with a calm that does not match the words: 'Devices collected at 7:45. Personal items reviewed weekly. Privileges earned through Trust.' She capitalizes Trust audibly. The paths divide here: “Refuse the device collection rule” leads into The Missing Kid, while “Accept it for tonight only” makes Your Daughter Whispers the next reckoning.

choices.text: Refuse the device collection rule
choices.consequence: Set one boundary they can't dissolve. You commit to refuse the device collection rule. It carries you into The Missing Kid while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Accept it for tonight only
choices.consequence: Pick the hill another day. You commit to accept it for tonight only. It carries you into Your Daughter Whispers while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Posters near the laundry room: a boy who 'graduated' six months ago, missing since the weekend. Evelyn whisks you past, talking too brightly about the dining hall. “Take a photo of the poster” draws you toward The Headmistress; “Pretend not to notice and keep watching” leaves After Lights Out waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Take a photo of the poster
choices.consequence: You commit to take a photo of the poster. It carries you into The Headmistress while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice and keep watching
choices.consequence: Cameras work both ways here. You pretend not to notice and keep watching. The way toward After Lights Out opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: She holds your sleeve at the dorm door and says, very quietly, 'Don't leave me here.' It is the first thing she has said to you with feeling in six months. “Walk her back to the car right now” draws you toward The Brochure; “Stay one night to see what they do” leaves The Headmistress waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Walk her back to the car right now
choices.consequence: Trust the kid you came to save. You choose to walk her back to the car right now. By The Brochure, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Stay one night to see what they do
choices.consequence: Knowledge is its own kind of rescue. You commit to stay one night to see what they do. It carries you into The Headmistress while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Helen Caplan — the founder — sits with you in a sunroom of plants you can't name. She is graceful, persuasive, terrifying in the way only kind voices can be. She knows your daughter's case file by heart.

choices.text: Match her calm and listen
choices.consequence: Underestimate her and you lose your daughter. You choose to match her calm and listen. By The Ally, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Push her for specifics about the missing kid
choices.consequence: Make her speak in particulars. You choose to push her for specifics about the missing kid. By The Office, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: From a window of the guest cabin you watch a small line of students walk in silence toward the woods at 1 a.m., escorted by counselors carrying flashlights. They return three hours later. The walk has a name. The walk does not have a permission slip.

choices.text: Follow them tomorrow night
choices.consequence: See it before you accuse it. You follow them tomorrow night. The way toward The Ally opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Photograph what you can right now
choices.consequence: Document while it's strange to you. You choose to photograph what you can right now. By The Office, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: A junior counselor named Abel meets your eye in a hallway and, on the way past, slides a folded napkin into your hand. 'Bridge. 11 p.m.,' it says. Either it's a trap or a lifeline. Maybe both.

choices.text: Meet him at the bridge
choices.consequence: Risk is sometimes the rescue. You commit to meet him at the bridge. It carries you into Bridge at Eleven while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Burn the napkin and stay alert
choices.consequence: Strangers in cults are rarely free agents. You commit to burn the napkin and stay alert. It carries you into Across the Lawn while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You slip into the records office on a long shot. Half the files are real, half are paper-thin theatre. You photograph three before voices come down the hall, and the door, when you try it, is locked.

choices.text: Hide in the closet
choices.consequence: Buy time at the cost of nerve. You hide in the closet. The way toward Bridge at Eleven opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Climb out the window onto the lawn
choices.consequence: Commit to escape before you're caught. You choose to climb out the window onto the lawn. By Across the Lawn, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Abel is younger than you thought, scared, and angry. He's been here since he was sixteen. 'They keep the ones who can't be sold back to families,' he says. “Promise to get him out too” draws you toward Your Daughter's Door; “Take the information and run” leaves Helen, Awake waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Promise to get him out too
choices.consequence: Save who you can, when you can. You choose to promise to get him out too. By Your Daughter's Door, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Take the information and run
choices.consequence: You commit to take the information and run. It carries you into Helen, Awake while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You sprint across the lit lawn with photos on a phone Helen will absolutely take in the morning if you let her. The guest cabin door is suddenly twenty miles away. A dog starts somewhere.

choices.text: Upload the photos to the cloud now
choices.consequence: Get it off you before it can be erased. You choose to upload the photos to the cloud now. By Your Daughter's Door, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Wipe the phone clean and rely on memory
choices.consequence: If they search you, find nothing. You commit to wipe the phone clean and rely on memory. It carries you into Helen, Awake while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You creep into the dorm and find her awake, alert, dressed. 'I knew you were coming back,' she says. She has been ready every night. To choose “Take her and as many girls as will come” means meeting The Run; “Take only her — keep this simple” sends you toward The Hostage Calm instead.

choices.text: Take her and as many girls as will come
choices.consequence: Rescue is contagious if you let it be. You choose to take her and as many girls as will come. By The Run, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Take only her — keep this simple
choices.consequence: A clean escape is its own miracle. You commit to take only her — keep this simple. It carries you into The Hostage Calm while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Helen is in the foyer in a robe like she's been waiting for you. She offers tea. She tells you, gently, that there is no version of this story where you are the hero. The distance between The Run and The Hostage Calm begins with the choice between “Refuse the tea and walk through her” and “Sit and let her speak — buy minutes.”

choices.text: Refuse the tea and walk through her
choices.consequence: Confidence is a passport. You commit to refuse the tea and walk through her. It carries you into The Run while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Sit and let her speak — buy minutes
choices.consequence: Sometimes the door opens behind you while she talks. You sit and let her speak — buy minutes. The way toward The Hostage Calm opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Down a gravel drive at 3 a.m. with your daughter and, somehow, four other girls in the back seat. Two trucks come up behind you, headlights on. The road is dark and long and yours.

choices.text: Outrun the trucks to the county line
choices.consequence: Cross a border, change the law you're under. You choose to outrun the trucks to the county line. By The County Line, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Cut off the road and use the back trails
choices.consequence: Wayward, weirdly, taught you these. You cut off the road and use the back trails. The way toward The Press opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Helen smiles. 'You can leave tonight,' she says, 'or your daughter can graduate next year. Choose.' The trick is that she means both versions. “Pretend to choose 'leave' and improvise” opens the route to The County Line. “Refuse her terms loudly enough to be heard outside” changes the terms and carries you toward The Press.

choices.text: Pretend to choose 'leave' and improvise
choices.consequence: You pretend to choose 'leave' and improvise. The way toward The County Line opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Refuse her terms loudly enough to be heard outside
choices.consequence: Witnesses are the cult's only allergen. You choose to refuse her terms loudly enough to be heard outside. By The Press, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You make it. The sun is coming up. Your daughter is asleep on the other girls' shoulders. The county sheriff's car flashes its lights and pulls you over — and the deputy at the window, blessedly, has never heard of Tall Pines.

choices.text: Tell him everything, now
choices.consequence: Truth told fast is a fence Helen can't climb. You tell him everything, now. The way toward Quietly Free opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Drive on with a story and seek a journalist
choices.consequence: Court of public opinion is faster than court of law. You choose to drive on with a story and seek a journalist. By The Headline, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: A reporter you cold-called from a gas-station pay phone agrees to meet at noon. She has been trying to crack Wayward for three years. You have, by accident, given her the headline. To choose “Go on the record with everything” means meeting The Headline; “Stay anonymous and trade documents only” sends you toward Quietly Free instead.

choices.text: Go on the record with everything
choices.consequence: Burn it down with paper and ink. You go on the record with everything. The way toward The Headline opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Stay anonymous and trade documents only
choices.consequence: Some safety is a smaller name. You choose to stay anonymous and trade documents only. By Quietly Free, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You don't enroll her. You drive eight more hours that night, with the brochure on the passenger seat, and start over the next morning at a different kind of help. Years later she tells you the only thing she's ever thanked you for is the night you turned around.

You and your daughter, and four girls you didn't know two days ago, end up in a small city far from Wayward. The investigation grinds slowly. You testify when asked. You sleep with the porch light on. You sleep.

The story breaks. Tall Pines closes inside a month. Helen Caplan is on three magazine covers and one indictment. Your daughter, who once would not look at you, sits beside you on a couch and squeezes your hand during the press conference.
